headline: Indian business remains resilient; European turnaround awaited

highlights: EBITDA, at INR 105bn, was in-line with our expectation (+18% YoY/+14% QoQ), supported by higher realisations and improved operating performance.

We expect H2FY27 performance to be even better, aided by INR 3,500–3,600/t QoQ rise in India realisations, higher volumes and operating leverage, partially offset by an ~USD 15/t increase in coking coal costs.
Over the long term, 4.8mnt of NINL expansion, downstream projects and third-party iron ore sales should drive growth, while debt is likely starts tapering in near term.

India remains robust; UK weakness persists Tata Steel reported consolidated EBITDA of INR 105.3bn, up 18% YoY/14% QoQ, supported by India performance and recovery in the Netherlands, partially offset by the subdued UK performance.
valuation: The Netherlands may benefit from stable DSP operations and higher contract realisations; in the UK, losses should narrow, as excess inventory gradually unwinds, with break-even targeted by Q4FY27.
Iron ore sales are targeted at 8–10mnt in FY27/14–15mnt in FY28, with captive mines expected to meet ~50% of requirements beyond 2030.
The company targets INR 70bn cost saving in FY27 (INR 18bn achieved in H1), alongside structural cost transformation programme through FY30.
watch: India-led capex and European recovery should support growth; leverage and execution are key monitorables.

Outlook: India-led expansion and downstream integration to drive growth; Europe remains a gradual recovery story Tata Steel is prioritising India-led capacity expansion, with the 4.8mnt NINL project targeted for commissioning by FY30, alongside the 0.7mnt HRPGL project and doubling of tinplate capacity.
